comment: No range is given for POS, REC POS, REC IN or the two outputs because the POS RANGE and I/O RANGE switches change them between 0 to 10V, ±5V and ±10V (Array.cpp:320-347). That also settles what a negative voltage does: on the ±5V and ±10V settings it is part of the span, and on the +10V setting it is clamped to the start of the array or the bottom of its value span (lines 350 and 369). No family is given for REC IN or the two outputs: the module stores and replays whatever voltage is given to it, so those jacks carry audio, CV or an envelope according to what is in the array. The SIZE box and the array display are plain widgets rather than parameters, so no click on them reaches this help; the drawing gesture and the SIZE box are covered by notes instead. Holding the platform modifier key while clicking the display leaves the array alone (Array.cpp:516-523). Arrays longer than 5000 values are saved beside the patch as a wav file rather than inside it.
